text:
Midday in Burlington and it's a gray, mid 40s kind of Tuesday, dry so far and a little raw with that damp air. The showers are waiting until later. Expect them to arrive around 4 and peak between 4 and 6, just as the sun sets near 4:30. They should taper off by about 7, and it's a light round, under a tenth of an inch. The afternoon high gets to about 51.

The models don't agree on this one. One keeps us mostly dry, while the European model and another run much wetter, so I'd keep the umbrella by the door for the commute home. Tonight clears out to a low near 39, with a breezy west wind.

Veterans Day looks mostly cloudy and mostly dry, with a high near 48. Thursday is the day to watch. A bigger system brings steadier rain, with highs in the low 40s.

week.blurb: Showers likely this afternoon and into the evening, ending around 10, with a high near 51 and only light amounts, so grab the umbrella.
Veterans Day stays dry and mostly cloudy with a high near 48, then a chilly night dipping into the mid 30s.
Clouds thicken with rain and a few wet flakes possible from morning on, high near 46, light amounts and nothing sticking.
Looks like a colder, gray Friday with a rain and snow mix possible on and off, high near 42, little to no accumulation.
Trending cloudy and cold with a high near 43, and a mix of rain and snow possible, though not a washout.
If the pattern holds, a leftover rain or snow shower early gives way to drier skies, with a high near 45.
Looks like the best sky of the stretch, partly sunny with a high near 46, then a cold night near 29.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -We are stuck in a very November-like pattern with clouds and mixed showers. Tuesday looks to start mainly dry, but showers start to make their return into Tuesday afternoon and evening, especially the further north you are. Some sunshine could emerge off to the south. Temperatures are in the 40s to lower 50s for Tuesday afternoon. Clouds remain stubborn all the way through midweek with mostly cloudy skies overhead for both Wednesday and Thursday. Temperatures start to turn a bit cooler, as they fall into the mid and upper 40s for Wednesday and the low to mid 40s for Thursday. Rain and higher elevation snow showers develop Thursday, especially by afternoon, as an area of low pressure approaches. Right now there is a question of how much of this can become accumulating snow outside of the mountains. We do turn drier into early next week, with mainly cloudy skies by Sunday and a few breaks of sunshine possible for Monday. Temperatures start to rebound a bit back into the low to mid 40s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-09T22:30:00Z — same caveat): Cloudy with additional showers Tuesday, brighter south — After a dry start to Tuesday, another round of scattered showers comes through by afternoon and evening, especially in northern areas. A few embedded downpours are possible. Highs reach the low 50s. More breaks of sun are likely in southern Vermont. Wednesday (Veterans Day) looks mostly dry, with only a spot shower or flurry possible. However, it will be mostly cloudy and chilly, with highs in the upper 40s. The late-week stretch looks quite chilly, as the jet stream dips farther south. Highs only reach the low to mid-40s, with lots of clouds. Rain and elevation snow showers develop Thursday, especially by afternoon, as an area of low pressure approaches. Depending on the storm track, a period of steadier rain and mountain snow is possible Friday, with mixed showers lingering into Saturday. Drier weather is likely early next week, followed by a warmup into the 50s.
